title: Study of Emotion Concept Formation by Integrating Vision, Physiology, and Word Information Using Multilayered Multimodal Latent Dirichlet Allocation
read_from: arXiv preprint 2404.08295 (published version: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing)
subcategory: multilayered multimodal LDA for concept formation
task: Modelling emotion-concept formation from interoceptive and exteroceptive signals
problem: Constructed-emotion theory says emotion concepts integrate internal and external information, but computational models of this formation are lacking.
architecture: Multilayered multimodal LDA (mMLDA) trained per subject with Gibbs sampling: an interoception module (EDA and heart-rate RRI signals discretised with pretrained VQ-VAE codebooks, K = 4) and exteroception modules (Inception-ResNet-v2 image features, K = 4; bag-of-words of the words subjects entered for each image, K = 34) integrated into a top concept layer (K = 28).

datasets.name: IAPS
datasets.details: 60 emotion-evoking images shown to 29 analysed subjects; 45 training and 15 test images for prediction

metrics: KL divergence of predicted vs actual modality distributions
key_results: Model categories match over 70% of subjects' self-reported categories, above the 0.56 chance level of the Rand index.
Unobserved physiology and word information predicted above chance; no significant difference between MLDA and mMLDA in similarity to reports.
strengths: Applies hierarchical multimodal topic models to non-text signals together with words.
Per-subject models with statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Bonferroni).

limitations.text: Category numbers set manually; only visual exteroception studied.
Small stimulus set (60 images) and 29 subjects.

notes: Included as a multimodal LDA application; words form one modality.
